subject: Post-call recap: model fit, benchmarks & next steps
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-07T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: model fit, benchmarks & next steps

Hi Emma —

Great to meet you and the team this morning. Quick recap + agreed next steps from our discovery:

Summary of goals:
- Conversational support assistant focused on technical troubleshooting for Acme's IoT products (short responses, high accuracy on product facts).
- 95th+ percentile latency target: sub-300ms for 256-token requests; tolerate up to 600ms p99 for heavier documents.
- Concurrent traffic profile: expected steady-state ~20 TPS with occasional spikes to 60 TPS during peak windows.

Model recommendations (based on today's prompts and your quality targets):
1) redwood/open-clarity-13b-quant (recommended starter) — best balance of latency/cost for short-context Q&A and high instruction-following fidelity.
2) open/llama-2-chat-70b (conservative fallback for the highest factual precision on long-context retrieval ops).
3) redwood/optimize-7b (ultra-low-cost option for high-TPS, less strict factual SLAs).

What I attached/linked below:
- Redwood-verified performance profiles (PDF) — per-model TPS and latency percentiles at 256/512/1024 tokens.
- redwood_benchmarks_acme_summary.csv — a short-run benchmark we discussed (synthetic traffic similar to your call traces).
- acme_prompt_set_v1.json — the prompt examples we ran during the call (please review and flag any PII or proprietary wording).

Quick numbers from the short-run benchmarks (256-token eval, single p4d-like instance profile):
- redwood/open-clarity-13b-quant: sustained throughput ~45 TPS (batching on), p50 75ms, p95 210ms, p99 320ms.
- redwood/optimize-7b: sustained throughput ~160 TPS, p50 25ms, p95 80ms, p99 140ms.
- open/llama-2-chat-70b: sustained throughput ~18 TPS, p50 120ms, p95 340ms, p99 620ms.

Next steps we agreed:
1) I'll share the benchmark artifacts and Redwood-verified profiles (attached + drive link).
2) Run a focused 1-hour benchmark with your real prompt set + a small subset of live traces (we recommend doing this in a dedicated environment).
3) Follow-up technical call with Dylan (solutions engineer) to walk results and discuss quantization/rolling strategies.

Proposed times for the follow-up: Tue or Wed next week — Dylan, can you confirm availability?

If that all looks right, I'll queue the benchmark and send a calendar invite for the follow-up call.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132

Attachments: redwood_benchmarks_acme_summary.csv, acme_prompt_set_v1.json, redwood-verified-performance-profiles.pdf

From: Emma Li <emma.li@acmecorp.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-03-07T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit, benchmarks & next steps

Thanks Alex — very helpful summary. A few clarifying Qs before we kick off the benchmark:

1) Can you share the p99 numbers specifically at 256 tokens when running at our expected concurrency profile (20 TPS steady, 60 TPS spikes)? The p99s you listed look great for single-instance runs but curious how they behave under realistic concurrency.
2) How does Redwood verify the "Redwood-verified" performance profiles? Is that an internal synthetic harness or do you run customer-specific traces?
3) We need the prompt set in a format our procurement/legal team can scan — can you confirm there's no customer PII in acme_prompt_set_v1.json?

Procurement wants a rough pricing delta between redwood/open-clarity-13b-quant and redwood/optimize-7b for the steady-state traffic (20 TPS). Can you include ballpark per-token or per-hour numbers?

Happy to run the focused 1-hour benchmark — we can provide a 1-minute sample of live traces for Dylan to seed the run.

Emma
Emma Li
Head of Product, Conversational AI | Acme Corp
emma.li@acmecorp.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-07T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit, benchmarks & next steps

Emma — great questions, answered inline below and with attachments/links.

1) p99 under realistic concurrency:
- We reran the 256-token benchmark with a concurrency profile targeting 20 TPS steady-state and 60 TPS spikes (bursting over ~2 minute windows) using Redwood Dedicated test harness configured to mirror your call traces. Results (aggregated across 3 runs):
  - redwood/open-clarity-13b-quant: steady p99 ~360ms; during 60 TPS burst p99 ~520ms.
  - redwood/optimize-7b: steady p99 ~150ms; burst p99 ~210ms.
  - open/llama-2-chat-70b: steady p99 ~550ms; burst p99 ~920ms.
Notes: the clarity-13b quantized variant shows increased p99 under bursty traffic because of KV-cache eviction patterns; we outline mitigations (burst autoscale, controlled batching) below.

2) What "Redwood-verified" means:
- We run a standardized verification harness (open-sourced benchmark code + internal orchestration) that exercises model RPCs with realistic token distributions and concurrency profiles. For customer-specific verification we:
  a) run the harness with your provided prompt set/traces in a dedicated, isolated environment;
  b) collect p50/p95/p99, throughput (TPS), and memory/KV metrics;
  c) validate correctness/regression by running your evaluation prompt set and scoring against expected outputs.
The PDF attached (redwood-verified-performance-profiles.pdf) includes the harness configuration and run reproducibility notes.

3) Prompt set & PII: we scanned acme_prompt_set_v1.json and sanitized anything that looked like customer identifiers. If you want, Dylan can walk legal/procurement through the schema and our redaction steps.

Pricing (ballpark for steady-state 20 TPS, 256-token avg):
- redwood/open-clarity-13b-quant: ~$3.50/hr (inference infra cost estimate) — ballpark per-token: ~0.0023 USD per token effective (depends on batching).
- redwood/optimize-7b: ~$1.10/hr — ballpark per-token: ~0.0008 USD per token.
Note: these are conservative infra estimates; final pricing depends on committed capacity, SLA tier, and data retention choices. Marissa (CC) can follow up with formal pricing/offer options for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Mitigations for p99 and burst behavior:
- Autoscale with short cool-down + burst buffer capacity to handle 2-3x spikes.
- Prefix/KV caching + sticky routing for conversational sessions to reduce KV cache churn.
- Drop-in fallback policy: start requests on redwood/open-clarity-13b-quant and auto-fallback to redwood/optimize-7b when queueing latency exceeds threshold.

Links & artifacts (attached and below):
- Benchmark viewer: https://app.redwood.ai/bench/view/RDW-ACME-2026-001
- Attached: redwood_benchmarks_acme_summary.csv (raw numbers), redwood-verified-performance-profiles.pdf (harness + profiles), acme_prompt_set_v1.json (sanitized prompt set).
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/RDW-ACME-2026-001

Next steps I'll take today:
- Schedule the 1-hour benchmark (Dylan to confirm time slot and env).
- Marissa to draft a pricing note and capacity/commit options.

Dylan — can you confirm you can run the focused benchmark tomorrow afternoon? Also please review the attached prompt set for any required redactions.

Thanks,
Alex
